title: CRUD
summary: CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) and RESTful API design while building a Pokedex-style API: POST, PUT/PATCH and DELETE methods in class-based views, and the right HTTP response for each one. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Add create, update and delete methods to DRF class-based views that follow REST conventions.

steps.title: Map Netflix actions to HTTP methods
steps.detail: Your Netflix app already does full CRUD; the Supabase client just hid the HTTP part. Add to My List is a create (POST), showing the list is a read (GET), changing a rating is an update (PATCH), removing a title is a delete (DELETE).
steps.doneWhen: Your notes have a 4-row table: action, HTTP method, expected status code.

steps.title: Read MDN's HTTP request methods
steps.detail: Skim GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on MDN.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain the difference between PUT and PATCH.

steps.title: Read DRF tutorial part 3
steps.detail: The class-based views tutorial shows `get`, `put` and `delete` methods side by side on one view.
steps.doneWhen: You can find the status code the tutorial returns after a delete (204).

concepts.meaning: Create, Read, Update, Delete: the four basic things an app does with data.
A style of API where URLs name resources and HTTP methods say what to do to them.
PUT replaces the whole record; PATCH changes only the fields you send.
The status code for a successful create.
The status code for success with nothing to send back, common after a delete.
